summary: A thin day: Reddit, Bluesky, Mastodon and most other sites were blocked from this environment, so only Hacker News yielded verifiable complaints. Strongest themes were remote job seekers outside the US/EU being filtered out by hidden country restrictions, developers left exposed by the eMudhra compromised-CA fallout, and people paying for streaming promos they forget to cancel.

ideas.title: Remote Jobs That Actually Hire in Your Country
ideas.oneLiner: A job board that only shows 'remote' roles you are legally and practically allowed to take from your own country, with a verified hiring-region tag.
ideas.problem: Postings say 'remote' but quietly restrict hiring to specific countries or economic zones because of payroll, tax and compliance rules. Candidates outside the US/EU burn weeks applying and only learn about the restriction on rejection.
ideas.targetUsers: Remote-seeking professionals in India, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines and other regions that are commonly excluded, plus the contractors and agencies that hire them.
ideas.monetization: Free browsing; ₹199–499/month for alerts, 'contractor-friendly' filters and an application tracker. Optional paid featured listings for employers who confirm they hire contractors in the candidate's country.
mvp: Aggregate public remote listings and parse the location text, flagging 'Worldwide', 'Americas only', 'EU timezone' and similar
Country picker with a clear 'can I be hired from here?' result per listing
Tag whether the employer says it hires contractors or only employees through an EOR
Email or push alert when a new role matches your country and skills
Report button so users can mark a listing that rejected them on location

competitors.name: General remote job boards (Remote OK, We Work Remotely, Remotive)
competitors.gap: Their 'worldwide' labelling is self-reported by employers, and candidates in the thread still report being rejected on location after applying.

competitors.name: LinkedIn Remote filter
competitors.gap: Treats 'remote' as a work-style flag and does not tell you which countries the employer can actually hire in.

sources.title: Why remote roles are becoming extinct in 2026?
sources.quote: I've been looking for new remote roles (marketing) for a while but there's no good role hiring remotely everywhere. I'm from India.

sources.title: Why remote roles are becoming extinct in 2026? (reply by rohansrma)
sources.quote: So, far I've applied to 75 jobs in two months and I got rejections just because of location issues.

sources.title: Why remote roles are becoming extinct in 2026? (reply by theafaid)
sources.quote: What's becoming less common is location-independent employment. Many companies still offer remote positions, but they increasingly restrict hiring to specific countries because of payroll, taxation, employment laws, and compliance.

sources.title: Why remote roles are becoming extinct in 2026? (reply by keiferski)
sources.quote: It's my impression that many of the roles that were previously "remote from anywhere in the world" are being replaced with either 1) a current employee using AI to be more productive or 2) a remote/partially remote job with the requirement to be in the same country/economic zone.

ideas.title: Trust-Store Drift Checker for Compromised CAs
ideas.oneLiner: A tiny CLI and menu-bar app that checks which of your tools (curl, git, Python, Node, browsers) still trust a distrusted CA, and re-checks after every OS update.
ideas.problem: After the compromise of eMudhra intermediate CAs, Apple blocked them for system frameworks, but command-line tools that read /etc/ssl/cert.pem still accept them. Manual fixes get silently undone by OS updates, and there is no easy way to see what is still exposed.
ideas.targetUsers: Developers, DevOps and security-minded teams on macOS and Linux, including the many in India who deal with eMudhra-issued certificates.
ideas.monetization: Free open-source CLI; paid team dashboard (about $5 per seat per month) that reports drift across a fleet of laptops and CI runners.
mvp: Maintained list of distrusted roots and intermediates, with a test endpoint per CA
Check curl, git, python3, node and system keychain, and report which still trust each CA
One-command remediation that sets SSL_CERT_FILE to a cleaned bundle
Re-run automatically after OS updates and warn if a previous fix was reverted
JSON output for CI and MDM tooling

competitors.name: Tanium and Konfirmity advisories and scripts
competitors.gap: One-off removal scripts for enterprises. They warn a later macOS update may restore the file, and nothing re-checks automatically for individual developers.

competitors.name: Apple's built-in distrust list
competitors.gap: Applies to Security.framework clients only. Apple says curl and git using /etc/ssl/cert.pem are not covered until a future update.

sources.title: Tell HN: The latest macOS Sequoia update seems to revert the eMudhra workaround
sources.quote: As far as I understand the macOS update has reinstalled the compromised certificates, and I have to re-apply the manual workaround again. I didn't expect that.

sources.title: Ten days later, Git on macOS still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificate (reply by RetroTechie)
sources.quote: If MacOS' setup somehow doesn't allow untangling a (still deemed trustworthy?!?) root certificate issued by eMudhra from the broken intermediate certificates, then revoke that whole chain including the root & accept collateral damage.

sources.title: macOS /etc/ssl/cert.pem still trusts the eMudhra roots: curl and python3 accept the compromised intermediates
sources.quote: Apple blocked the eight compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs (CVE-2026-111943) for Security.framework clients. But on macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), `/usr/bin/curl` and `/usr/bin/python3` still accept certificates from them.

ideas.title: Promo and Trial Expiry Cancel Reminder
ideas.oneLiner: A one-time-purchase, on-device app that tracks discounted streaming deals and free trials and nudges you with the cancel link a few days before the price jumps.
ideas.problem: People take introductory deals and trials, forget to cancel, and pay for months. Existing subscription trackers are themselves subscriptions that people then forget to cancel.
ideas.targetUsers: Streaming and app-subscription users, especially in India where UPI autopay mandates renew silently, and anyone who rotates between services for deals.
ideas.monetization: Free for 3 reminders; one-time unlock of ₹199 / $4.99, with no recurring plan.
mvp: Add a deal in two taps with service, price after promo, and end date
Local notifications 7, 3 and 1 day before the deal ends
Built-in cancel deep links for the top 50 services
Share-sheet import from confirmation emails and SMS, processed on device
Monthly 'money saved by cancelling' summary

competitors.name: TrialGuard (iOS)
competitors.gap: Reminders only, and no India-specific UPI mandate awareness.

competitors.name: TrialMinder / TrialPing (Chrome extensions)
competitors.gap: Desktop-only, so reminders do not reach you where you actually cancel (the phone), and the free plan is capped at a few reminders.

sources.title: Disney Raising Prices Days After Confirming Ads Will Now Show (comment by nswizzle31)
sources.quote: Just like I did for Fox One during the World Cup and then 4 months and $120 later I remember to cancel it. Then I pay for a subscription for a tool to remind me to cancel subscriptions and forget to cancel that one too.

sources.title: Disney Raising Prices Days After Confirming Ads Will Now Show (comment by aaronbrethorst)
sources.quote: I canceled after year 2, and rejoined when I got an offer to pay $5/month for the ads tier this past November. I'll be canceling in a couple weeks when that deal expires.

ideas.title: Free Source Finder for Paywalled Articles
ideas.oneLiner: When you open a paywalled news link, the extension finds legitimate free coverage of the same story (wire copies, syndication, primary sources) and shows it beside the original.
ideas.problem: Readers and community moderators want to share news links that everyone can read. Bypass sites are shady and inconsistent, and a headline alone is often all the discussion has to go on.
ideas.targetUsers: Forum and newsletter users who share links, and readers who hit several paywalls a day.
ideas.monetization: Free tier with a few lookups a day; $3/month for unlimited lookups and a share-link generator that bundles the open alternatives.
mvp: Detect a paywalled page and extract the story's key entities and headline
Search syndication partners, wire services and primary documents for matching free coverage
Side panel with ranked free alternatives and a similarity score
One-click share link that lists the open sources instead of the paywalled one
Allow-list of reputable sources so results are not scraped junk

competitors.name: archive.today and similar snapshot sites
competitors.gap: The only workaround people trust, but one commenter calls it shady because the text could be altered later, and links are inconsistent.

competitors.name: Ground News and similar aggregators
competitors.gap: Built for comparing coverage, not for finding a freely readable copy of the exact story from a link you are about to share.

sources.title: Ask HN: Should something be done about paywalled articles?
sources.quote: Sometimes big news will end up paywalled and an often subjective HN title is all you have to work with.

sources.title: Archive.today links going forward (comment by ada-h00k)
sources.quote: The only reason people use such dubious sites is that there's no other way to share a link to a news site without risking that the text will be altered later or hidden behind a paywall.
